name: hra-cell-types
title: HRA Cell-Type Term Occurrences
question:
Does the HRA CCF API's cell-type-term-occurences endpoint load into a
Step-driven composite, giving a Cell Ontology (CL) term occurrence list?

study_card.goal: Fetch HRA cell-type term occurrences via HRACellTypesStep and confirm the composite loads a non-empty, count-sorted CL term list.
study_card.expected_result: Cell Ontology terms load as CURIEs sorted by occurrence count descending.
study_card.main_expert_question: Which CL terms dominate the HRA corpus, and do they align with the organs we care about for glucose regulation (pancreas, liver, adipose, muscle)?

biological_summary:
The HRA's cell-type-term-occurrence histogram counts, across every HRA
dataset (tissue block, single-cell, spatial), how often each Cell
Ontology (CL) term is annotated on a cell population. A term's occurrence
count is a proxy for how broadly that cell type has been profiled across
organs/datasets, not for its abundance in the body — a near-universal
term (e.g. an ontology root) will out-rank a rare-but-important cell type
like a pancreatic beta cell simply because it is annotated on almost
every dataset.

report.title: HRA Cell Types — 149 distinct CL terms loaded, top term at 2,762 occurrences
report.objective:
Does the HRA CCF API's cell-type-term-occurences endpoint load into a
Step-driven composite, giving a Cell Ontology (CL) term occurrence
list?
report.conclusion:
A live run against
`https://apps.humanatlas.io/api/v1/cell-type-term-occurences` returned
149 distinct CL terms, sorted by occurrence count descending. The top
term (CL:0000000) occurs 2,762 times — an order of magnitude above the
#2-#9 tier, which cluster at exactly 266 occurrences each (CL:0010008,
CL:0000084, CL:0000236, CL:0000576, CL:0000623, CL:0011005, CL:4023011,
CL:4023016), suggesting those co-occur as a fixed per-record annotation
bundle in whatever HRA datasets contribute them.
report.caveat:
The dominant top term (2,762 occurrences, ~4x the next tier) reads as a
broad/root-level CL annotation rather than a specific, glucose-relevant
cell type — this endpoint answers "which CL terms are most annotated
across HRA datasets", not "which cell types matter most for glucose
regulation" (pancreatic beta cells, hepatocytes, adipocytes do not
appear in the top 10 by this measure).
